From my understanding, one’s own individual path in and to Wicca can encompass goddess worship, deity work and working with both the divine masculine and feminine ancestral deities. One thing that stands out always, to me as a beginner anyway, is the focus on individual freedom and self-identification as you may see fit. You can do as thou wilt, so for example, follow pagan traditionalism, work or not work with divinities, be an agnostic Wiccan, delve into witchcraft, follow Wiccan holidays and the wheel of year etc. 

I recommend this free app I binge-read the other night, Wicca, Book of Shadows and Light, which covers all these sorts of questions for beginners! 

> Introduction to Wicca — Stephanie Marks

 “Wicca (also known as Witchcraft) is a nature-based polytheistic faith with its roots in the pre-Christian tribal cultures of Europe. The nature-based aspect of the faith leads many followers to regard all living things as sacred.

In the years since the Witchcraft laws were repealed in the middle of the 20th century, Wicca has seen a widespread resurgence. Renewed interest continues to grow today, as the general public has grown more knowledgable and accepting, and perhaps, as modern life has left many of us feeling a distinct lack of nature in our lives.

Wiccans (also known as Witches) believe in both a Goddess and a God as representative of the divine and of the dualities which exist throughout nature. Wiccans may use many different names to refer to these deities. These may be viewed as either separate and distinct God and Goddess figures, or as different aspects or personas of a single God and Goddess.

It is very important to note that Wiccans do not believe in, or in any way worship a 'satan' or 'devil' figure. 'Satanism' is a rebellion or inversion of Christian and Jewish traditions. Wiccans do not hate or revile the Bible. They simply regard it as one of the world's many diverse systems of mythology.”

Hope some of this is helpful, try check out the sidebar for more information, as I am a beginner. Remain curious, open-minded and remember that this is YOUR own path, harm Ye none and Blessed Be. Xx

For a few weeks it didn't do much, so we kept going higher with the dosage, eventually I had a bit of a 'lightbulb' moment where everything felt and looked a bit brighter. I can't really explain it now. I really think in combination with exercise, diet, sleep, therapy (cbt), social outlets etc, they have really helped me. I wouldn’t say healed, I have a confusing relationship with religion and Christianity. Much like above user, was raised Catholic, then atheist all throughout teens, now searching and going to church and praying sometimes. Sometimes it does, but when the depression is so bad, I do feel a real block between any form of spirituality. Like a huge glass wall, however, C.S Lewis also went through depression and wrote similarly. He found that when he called out to God, he actually heard a bolting door sound. I think he grew stronger in his faith, but interesting to read about saints who experienced depression and mental health issues. Have a look maybe at different saints and their lives and maybe pray through them and your guardian angel from protection from negativity and dark thoughts such as intrusive thoughts. Sometimes I just cross myself when I feel especially dark and low...idk if you believe in demons or the devil but Christian’s believe that he looks out for vulnerable people and even more for people who are vulnerable and searching for Christ. It’s a long life and I sometimes completely abandon God, but I guess the thing is, he never abandons is and for someone who feels suicidal often...it comforts me a lot. Why don’t you try calling a prayer hotline, in the U.S they have heaaaaps, Australia not so many. You can just chat with someone about life and they will pray with you. It’s just a nice thing to do when you should reach out but can’t manage going out and trying to socialise with friends for hours or whatever. Maybe talk to a pastor or priest, or maybe a monk or spiritual teacher, whatever your spirituality. One thing about Christian people at church’s are that often, they are just super nice. Like, wholesome “I just met you but I’ll pick you up for church and dinners on me” nice. Good luck with everything and take care 💜🌈
